orrowen: Cadhan o hosen re yal cadhat lona
meanings: This we (two) lay as it was laid for us (two): Halyna's close to every telling of theirs, the dual of O0234
derivation: a phrase: Cadhan lay-1DU + o it(+S) + hosen as + re PST(+S) + yal S·be.PST + cadhat laid + lona at-1DU; the dual of O0234 (Cadhar ... lor), because the Bonded speak of themselves as 'we two' and where the Book gives Halyna a plural verb the Orrowen original is dual (orrowen_v2 §3.9 item 1; the Stonwryt's own re hadhan o, §11.6); unit S02 (I.4)
logogram: TRENN+still (43) + A n · TRENN+still (43) + A t
book_lemmas: This we lay as it was laid for us

meanings: the Bonded of the Keep: Halyna's title
derivation: a phrase: Lodhan the Bonded (lodh + -an, canon, 'those of the mortar') + et the + Kethow keep; a construct, its head without the article (orrowen_v2 §3.2), the possessor definite; unit S02 (I.4)
a phrase: Hale (canon name; names are names) + haskard 'a runner' (canon: hask + -Ard); apposition, as Kael Nydherd (orrowen_v2 §3.10); unit S02 (I.3)

meanings: Commander of Rivenkeep: the name the Rite gave the Captain
derivation: a phrase: Ketherd the Commander (canon: keth + -Ard, 'the holder') + Hethow Dhresk, Kethow Dhresk softened as the possessor of a construct (k > h; orrowen_v2 §3.2, as lest Vardh); NB Hethow also reads as heth 'spring' + -ow (lexicon §8.2 finding 2); Dhresk after it settles the reading; unit S02 (I.4)

orrowen: Lo et Crenn, clem sell hosen orl
meanings: For the Captain, an hour lasts as long as a day: the wall's saying (I.3); 'at the Captain, an hour long as a day'
derivation: a phrase: lo at(+S) + et the + Crenn captain + clem hour + sell long + hosen as + orl day; verbless, as Orrowen proverbs are (orrowen_v2 §11.7); unit S02 (I.3)
book_lemmas: an hour lasts as long as a day

meanings: the laying: the hour of the siege day when the Stonewrights raise and mend
derivation: a phrase: et the + cadhol laying (cadh + -Ol, tier3 O0237); the siege day's first hour by its work; unit S02 (I.3)

meanings: the hauling: the hour of the siege day when the guns are dragged to where the Captain wants them
derivation: a phrase: et the + caldol hauling (cald + -Ol, O0243); always said with its article: after ul (+N) the bare caldol would bed to galdol 'building', and after lo (+S) soften to haldol, heard as hald 'wall' (lexicon §8.2 finding 2); unit S02 (I.3)

meanings: the holding: the hour of the siege day when the grey sails come in and the wall must stand
derivation: a phrase: et the + kethyl holding (canon: keth + -Ol); the hour is named for the canon's own verb of the wall and of the Captain (Ketherd, 'the holder'); unit S02 (I.3)

meanings: course upon course: a paragraph each, by turns (of a telling laid in two inks)
derivation: a phrase: trenn course, line, tale + um upon(+S) + dhrenn S·trenn (t > dh), shaped on the Cry's tolm um dholm (orrowen_v2 §11.2); unit S02 (I.4 headnote)
a phrase: bystir a stair (reserve) + um upon(+S) + wystir S·bystir (b > w), as tolm um dholm; unit S02 (I.4)
a phrase: hoss breath (canon) + kethet held (keth + -At); the breath of the title Hoss Sell et Crenn, let out; unit S02 (I.3)
a phrase: vess night + ull that, as orl ull 'that day' (O2865) and vess sy; unit S02 (I.4)

meanings: done, made (the participle of gald in its senses 'do, make'); of a rite: done, performed (re yal et Ternil galdat, 'the Rite was done'); a thing done
derivation: gald 'build, raise a work; do, make' (O0655, canon) + -At (participle), broad -at. SENSE ROW for O0657 galdat, not a new lemma: O0657 gives the participle only the verb's first sense ('built, raised a work'), so a blind reader read vodh re yal galdat lo as 'what was built with it' (the lexicon builder gives a participle only its verb's base sense, as backtrans_I1 §7 item 2 found for driget). Orchestrator: merge these senses into O0657. Unit S02 (I.4 P1, P5, P10), blind back-translation wf8/backtrans/S02.md
